tasks.short: Train faculty and media staff on software and audio-visual equipment

steps.what: Read which software and equipment the session covers
Decide which software and equipment faculty will practise
Train faculty and media staff on the audio-visual equipment
Write the session handout and the agreed time
File the accepted session handout in the library store
File the accepted session time on the library calendar

tasks.design: She still trains faculty and media staff in the room and tells them the time there. After she accepts the session handout, {DOCS} files that version and {CALENDAR} files the date and time written on it. Neither step sends a message, and the session is not recorded.
tasks.previous_blocker: The handout sat in her own notes, and the agreed time was easy to lose after she left the room.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store and a calendar can each file the version she has already accepted. The teaching itself needs no model.
tasks.still_hard: People learn this equipment by using it with her. A filed handout does not replace the session.
tasks.human_edge: She sees who is lost and changes the exercise while they are still in the room.
tasks.altitude: She still runs the session and still decides the exercises. She no longer copies the handout into a second folder.

reach.task: Set up audio-visual equipment for a training session
reach.learn: Which software and equipment the accepted handout names, and the time she filed.

evidence.claim: A document store and a calendar can file a handout and a time she has already accepted. That filing does not shorten the training.
Works-council consent is needed if a system logs output to check a cataloguer's work.

assumptions: In s4 she types the handout fields herself: topic, software names, equipment names, room, date and time. The handout has no attendance list and no score of her teaching.
She produces that handout in s4. If the training request was only spoken, the scope she noted in s1 is the input, and the typing still sits in s4.
s5 files the handout version she accepted in s4. s6 files the date and time from that same version. A later edit voids both filings.
She tells faculty and media staff the time during s3. s6 does not send a message. Both are colleagues in the same organisation.
The session is not recorded, so the filing is not a log of her teaching.
Upkeep is 2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task: a few times a year a room name or a software title on the form changes, and that edit is not part of the session.
unknowns: Whether she currently writes a handout at all, or only demonstrates and leaves.
Whether the works council treats a stored handout as a check on her teaching.
research_questions: Does a session handout today already have separate fields for topic, equipment, room and time, or is it one free note?

already_counted.description: She rereads the handout in s4 and accepts it before either filing runs.

incremental.description: A few times a year she updates a room name or a software title on the handout form.

approvals.approved_version: session handout she accepted in s4
session handout she accepted in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If she still recopies the handout after the session, the two filings save nothing that day. If she accepts once and both filings use that version, the high stays at 2, under the net, because some sessions have no written handout.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain the inventory of audio-visual equipment

steps.what: Read the current inventory of audio-visual equipment
Count the audio-visual equipment in each room
Decide which audio-visual equipment is missing or for repair
Write the accepted counts for the audio-visual inventory
File the accepted audio-visual equipment inventory

tasks.design: She still walks the rooms and writes each count. {OTHER} (equipment inventory) files the version she accepts, with name, room, count and status. It does not read labels and it does not order equipment.
tasks.previous_blocker: After the walk she retyped the same counts onto a second list.
tasks.enabler_now: A records list can store the counts she has already typed and accepted. No model has to read the labels.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see each item. A missing label, or an item that is out with a class, is her call.
tasks.human_edge: She can tell a missing projector from one that is in use in a class.

ambition.what: Mark one item for repair in the week it fails, instead of waiting for the next full count.

tasks.altitude: She still walks the rooms and still decides what is missing or for repair. The second copy of the list is filed from the counts she accepted.

reach.learn: Which items she marked missing or for repair, and the room on the accepted count.

evidence.claim: A records list can store equipment counts a person has typed, with name, room, count and status. It does not need a model to read labels.

assumptions: In s4 she types the fields herself: equipment name, room, count as an integer, and status as present, missing or repair. The row has no staff name.
She produces those fields in s4 from the count she made in s2. An item with no readable label gets a name she types in s4, and that time stays in s4.
The list she reads in s1 is the last filed inventory from this same task, or an empty list the first time. s5 files only the version she accepted in s4.
s5 does not order replacements and does not send a message to a supplier or a colleague.
A one-item status change uses the same s4 and s5 path. It does not shorten the room-by-room count in s2.
Upkeep is 2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task: a few times a year a room name or a status value on the form changes, outside the walk.
unknowns: Whether this equipment already sits in a collection system, or only on a shelf list she retypes.
Whether finance keeps the same items on an asset register.
research_questions: Does the current list already store equipment name, room, count and status as separate fields?

already_counted.description: In s4 she checks odd counts, such as a room she could not enter, before she accepts the list.

incremental.description: A few times a year she adds a room name or a status value on the inventory form.

approvals.approved_version: equipment count she accepted in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If she still counts on paper and retypes every row, the filing saves nothing that day. If she enters each count once and the filing uses that version, the high stays at 6, under the net, because new items are still typed in full in s4.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Hear the problems reported for the audio-visual equipment
Troubleshoot the audio-visual equipment and name the fault
Fix the audio-visual equipment or set it aside
Tell the colleague the result for the audio-visual equipment
Write the accepted fault note for the audio-visual equipment
File the accepted fault note on the audio-visual equipment

tasks.design: She still finds the fault at the set and tells the colleague in the room. {OTHER} (equipment inventory) files the fault note she accepts, with the name, what failed, what she did, and whether it is still down. No model suggests the fault, and the note does not score her work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The fix stayed in her memory, so the next person repeated the same checks.
tasks.enabler_now: The equipment inventory can hold the short note she has already accepted. Naming the fault still needs her at the set.
tasks.still_hard: The fault is on that set, that day. A manual does not show a loose cable behind a podium.
tasks.human_edge: She tries the set and knows when to stop and mark it down.
tasks.altitude: She still finds and fixes the fault, and she still tells the colleague in the room. The note is filed once.

reach.task: Plan a class that needs audio-visual equipment
reach.learn: Which items her accepted fault note still marks as down.

evidence.claim: An equipment inventory can store a fault note a person has typed. A model is not used here to name the fault.
Works-council consent is needed if a system logs output to check a cataloguer's work.
No Annex III area of the EU AI Act applies to this occupation's work.

assumptions: The person who reports the fault is a colleague in the same organisation. Telling them the result in s4 is an internal conversation. s4 sends nothing, and it is not a message to someone outside.
In s5 she types the note herself: equipment name, what failed, what she did, and still down as yes or no. The note has no score of her work.
The equipment name matches a row from the inventory task when that row exists. If it does not, she types the name in s5, and that time stays in s5.
s6 files only the note she accepted in s5. It does not send a message. A later edit voids the filing.

Upkeep is 1 hour per 100 baseline hours of this task: occasional cleanup of the still-down value and the short fault phrases. Many faults are fixed and never written down, so the allowance stays small.
unknowns: Whether a fault is written down today, or only fixed and then forgotten.
Whether a works council would treat the fault note as a check on her work if a manager later read it that way.
research_questions: Does the equipment inventory already have a place for a short fault note, or only a name and a room?

already_counted.description: In s5 she rereads the fault note and accepts it before the filing runs.

incremental.description: Occasional cleanup of the still-down flag and the short fault phrases on the note.

approvals.approved_version: fault note she accepted in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Many faults are fixed in the room and never written down, so the filing saves nothing. When she does accept a note, filing it once is the high, kept at 1, under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still trains faculty in the room, still counts the equipment, and still finds the fault. The handout, the counts, and the fault note are each filed once from the version she accepted.
skills_to_grow: Writing a session handout another person can follow
Recording equipment status in fixed fields
role.ambitious_version: A technician can see an item marked for repair the week it fails, and the session handout she accepted is on file with its time.
